title: Per-cluster GPU scheduling and cost allocation runbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:

This runbook documents the operational patterns we use at Redwood for per-cluster GPU scheduling, multi-account/network segmentation, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD for GPU node and image builds, and the step-by-step actions for handling capacity shortages or noisy tenants. It is intended for oncall engineers, infra owners, SREs, and platform engineers who manage GPU-backed K8s clusters (hosted, Dedicated, and Private).

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Ensure predictable scheduling, fair cost allocation, and fast recovery when GPU capacity problems occur.
- Scope: Applies to all GPU-capable clusters managed by eng-infra (GKE/AKS/EKS) and to Dedicated customer pools. Does not cover batch/spark clusters (separate doc).

Owners and contacts:
- Primary owner: eng-infra/gpu-capacity (pager: #infra-gpu on Slack)
- Secondary owner: eng-sre-oncall
- Runbook author: Priya Nair
- Recommended reviewers for changes: Platform, CostOps, Security

Architecture summary (high level):
- Each cloud account maps to one or more cluster clusters (dev/prod/customer-dedicated).
- GPU node pools are created per-tenant group with clear tagging (see Tagging schema).
- Scheduling model uses: node taints + tolerations for isolation, node selectors/affinity for placement, and PriorityClass for preemption ordering.
- Autoscaling: Cluster Autoscaler + custom topology-aware scaler for burst windows.
- Billing: Cloud labels -> billing export -> BigQuery/Cost Center.

Tagging and account segmentation (table):
- Tagging schema (required labels on node pools and instances):

| Key | Purpose | Example |
|-----|---------|---------|
| redwood:env | environment | prod, staging, dev |
| redwood:team | owning team | search, docs, evals |
| redwood:workload | workload intent | realtime-inference, batch-eval |
| redwood:billing_code | cost center | BI-1234 |
| redwood:dedicated_customer | if dedicated | customer-acme |

(We require these tags in Terraform modules; enforcement via pre-commit policy and Terraform plan checks.)

Scheduling patterns and policies:
1) Strong isolation (recommended for customer-dedicated):
   - Node pools per-customer with taint key gpu-isolated:NoSchedule.
   - Pods use tolerations: allow only pods with redwood:dedicated_customer label to schedule.
2) Shared inference pools (cost-efficient):
   - Use nodeSelector redwood:workload=realtime-inference and priorityClass inference-high.
   - Set PodDisruptionBudget minAvailable: 90% for SLO-sensitive services.
3) Best-effort/Batch pools (low-cost):
   - Use preemptible/spot instances. Mark with label preemptible=true and PriorityClass batch-low.

Kubernetes examples (YAML snippets):

Taint a node pool (example using gcloud):
```
# Add a taint during node pool creation (GKE example)
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-pool-x --cluster=prod-cluster --machine-type=n1-standard-16 --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 --node-taints=gpu-isolated:NoSchedule --labels=redwood:workload=realtime-inference
```

Pod toleration example:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: realtime-model
  labels:
    app: model
spec:
  containers:
  - name: model
    image: us-docker.pkg.redwood/model-serving:latest
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu-isolated"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  nodeSelector:
    redwood:workload: realtime-inference
  priorityClassName: inference-high
```

Autoscaler configuration and thresholds (table):

| Component | Metric | Alert threshold | Action |
|-----------|--------|-----------------|--------|
| Node pool autoscaler | GPU utilization (avg 5m) | > 80% for 10m | Scale up pool by +1 node or trigger burst request to Dedicated capacity API |
| Pending pods queue | count waiting for GPU | > 5 pods for 5m | Increase pool size, or notify owners, apply emergency migration to shared-pool |
| GPU fragmentation ratio | % GPUs partially used | > 30% | Recommend consolidation: evict low-priority batch jobs, run packing cron job |

Terraform / IaC patterns and modules:
- Modules: we maintain `modules/gpu-node-pool`, `modules/gpu-iam-and-tags`, `modules/gpu-bastion`, and `modules/gpu-network` in the infra mono-repo.
- Module contracts: every module must accept `labels`, `billing_code`, and `tenant` variables and emit `node_pool_id` and `instance_group_name`.
- Pre-deploy checks: `tfsec` + `checkov`, `terraform validate`, `terraform plan` + approval. Enforce tagging with a policy (policy-as-code runs in CI).

Terraform example (minimal):
```
module "gpu_node_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.redwood/infra/modules//gpu-node-pool"
  cluster = "prod-cluster"
  machine_type = "n1-highmem-16"
  accelerator = { type = "nvidia-tesla-a100", count = 1 }
  labels = { "redwood:env" = "prod", "redwood:team" = "search", "redwood:billing_code" = "AI-202" }
}
```

CI/CD: images and node pool IaC pipeline:
- Image build pipeline (images/gpu) triggers on commits to `infra/images/gpu` and runs: build -> container-scan -> push to registry -> trigger canary rollout. SLO: image build < 30m.
- IaC pipeline: `ci/terraform` runs `terraform plan` in PR, policy checks, and requires 2 approvals for prod apply. Production applies are gated and require a runbook reference in the PR description.

Operational runbook: capacity shortage event (high severity)
1) Detect: Alert triggers for "pending pods waiting for GPU > 5" or "GPU utilization > 90% for 15m". Pager to #infra-gpu.
2) Triage: owner oncall to run immediate checks:
   - Check cluster state: `kubectl get nodes -o wide`
   - Check pending pods: `kubectl get pods -A -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Pending`
   - Check Cloud autoscaler events (GKE): `gcloud container operations list --filter="operationType=UPGRADE_NODE_POOL"` (or equivalent API)
3) Quick mitigations (choose in order):
   a) Increase node pool size by +1 via Terraform quick variable change (use `tf apply -var 'desired_size=+1'` in a pre-authorized emergency workspace).
   b) Failover non-critical tenants: move batch jobs to preemptible pools (apply label migration).
   c) Burst to Dedicated API: if configured, call internal dedicated-capacity API endpoint `POST /internal/dedicated/burst` with payload {"cluster":"prod","gpu_count":2}.
4) Longer term: run packing job to reduce fragmentation, investigate noisy tenant.

Handling preemption and spot interruptions:
- For preemptible pools, use a two-second shutdown handler in the image to checkpoint model state. Add `lifecycle` hooks to trigger draining: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --timeout=5m <node>` after spot termination notice.
- Monitor spot termination rate; alert if > 10% of pool over rolling 1h.

Runbook for noisy tenant (quality degradation / high variance):
1) Identify top GPU consumers with `kubectl top pods --containers` and `gcloud compute instances list --filter='labels.redwood:team~.*' --format=json` for cloud-specific heat maps.
2) Throttle by creating a ResourceQuota in the tenant namespace:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: gpu-quota
  namespace: noisy-tenant
spec:
  hard:
    nvidia.com/gpu: "2"
```
3) If the tenant continues to destabilize, evict pods (priority-based) and schedule a tenant remediation call.

Metrics, SLOs and alerting (concrete):
- SLOs:
  - 95th percentile scheduling latency for GPU pods <= 30s (prod clusters).
  - Avg GPU utilization target: 45–75% (to balance cost & latency).
- Key metrics to emit to Datadog/Prometheus: gpu_utilization_pct, gpu_pending_pod_count, gpu_fragmentation_ratio, node_pool_scale_events, preemptible_termination_rate.
- Alert routing: critical -> #infra-gpu (pager), warning -> #infra-gpu-watch, billing anomalies -> CostOps.

Change and rollout process (short):
1) Create infra PR with terraform plan output and runbook link.
2) Run preflight in staging cluster.
3) Apply to canary node pool (non-prod) and validate metrics for 24h.
4) Apply to prod node pools with rolling replacement (maxUnavailable: 1 node per pool).
5) Post-change validation: confirm scheduling latency within SLO and check cost delta in billing export for 48h.

Post-incident actions (postmortem checklist):
- Owner files a short incident review with timeline, root cause, remediation, and follow-up action items within 72h.
- Add IaC tests that would have prevented the issue (e.g., enforce sane autoscaler min/max).

Appendix: quick commands and snippets
- List all GPU node pools (GKE):
```
gcloud container node-pools list --cluster=prod-cluster --filter="config.accelerators.type:*"
```
- Pending pods query (Kubernetes):
```
kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o=jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name}:{.spec.nodeName}
'{end}
```
- Emergency scale (Terraform workspace pattern):
```
# Use pre-authorized workspace `infra-emergency`
tf workspace select infra-emergency
terraform apply -var 'cluster=prod-cluster' -var 'emergency_scale=2'
```

Related pages and governance:
- See GPU fleet metrics runbook for alert definitions and dashboards.
- All IaC changes must include a labels matrix and cost center in PR description.

Revision history:
- 2024-03-12: Created by Priya Nair
- 2024-10-02: Added tagging enforcement details and module contract
- 2025-11-20: Expanded CI/CD pipeline section and added emergency API burst step

If you see missing steps or have suggested improvements, please open a PR against infra/runbooks and add reviewers from the reviewers list.
